subject: On‑prem observability: certificates, HEC handoff, and tracing headers
messages:
From: John Miller <jmiller@acmecorp.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: SecOps Team <secops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2029 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Observability export for on‑prem Redwood deployment - questions

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the onboarding docs so far. We're prepping the on‑prem/VPC deployment and SecOps has a few specific questions about how Redwood will hand observability out of our environment into our SIEM (Splunk):

1) TLS / certs: do you support mutual TLS to Splunk HEC? If not, what cert rotation cadence and automation do you recommend?
2) Egress & networking: which IP ranges and ports do we need to allow (HEC, metrics push, traces)? Is the service able to retry across multiple egress addresses?
3) Long‑lived connections: for tracing hooks and metrics, do you use a persistent (long) TCP connection or short lived HTTP posts?
4) Tokens & secrets: how often should HEC tokens rotate and do you support dynamic token injection from our KMS?
5) Trace context: which headers do you propagate (traceparent, b3, x-cloud-trace-context)? We need to map this to our APM.
6) Data residency & retention: logs that contain PII — can we apply scrub rules on the Redwood side before egress? We also need evidence for audit (who forwarded, when).

Can you send a short checklist and a network diagram showing the handoff path? We have a compliance review next week.

— John
John Miller
SecOps Lead, AcmeCorp
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

John — thanks for the clear list. Goal: give you an executable handshake plan and the artifacts your audit team needs. High level answers below; Marissa and Mina will follow up with the runbook and checklist. I've attached a draft VPC flow diagram for review.

Short answers:
- TLS / certs: we support mTLS to customer HEC endpoints for Private deployments (recommended). If you prefer HEC tokens, we recommend automated rotation every 30–90 days; we can integrate with your KMS for on‑deploy token injection.
- Egress: primary is HTTPS to HEC (port 8088 commonly), metrics push via HTTPS (443) and trace exporter HTTP/HTTPS depending on collector. We'll provide precise CIDR list for allowlisting.
- Connections: exporter uses persistent HTTP/1.1 keepalive pools for metrics/HEC to reduce connection churn; trace hooks generally POST spans (batching) over TLS.
- Token management: support for ephemeral tokens via KMS + short TTL if you want aggressive rotation.
- Trace context: we propagate traceparent and support b3; we'll include a header matrix.
- Scrubbing: Redwood Private supports pre‑egress scrubbing rules and field redaction policies; we'll include example scrub rules and a proof bundle mechanism for audits.

Next steps: Marissa will share the Splunk HEC runbook and exact CIDR/IPs. Mina will provide the compliance checklist and sample evidence bundle. Can you do a 30‑minute handshake on Mon Jul 29? We can propose 11:00–11:30 UTC.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

John / team — following up with concrete specifics and a proposed minimal configuration for your Splunk ingest. Attaching a lightweight runbook (splunk_hec_runbook.md) and a trace header matrix (tracehook_header_matrix.csv). Highlights below: 

1) mTLS vs HEC token:
   - mTLS: recommended for highest assurance. Redwood supports client certs (PEM) pinned at the forwarder. Cert rotation: 90 days recommended; we can automate issuance via your internal CA if you provide an API endpoint.
   - HEC tokens: supported as bearer tokens. If using tokens, set rotation to 30 days and enable token reuse detection on your side.

2) Network and ports:
   - HEC (splunkd) endpoint: TCP/8088 (HTTPS) — allow from our forwarder IP pool.
   - Metrics push (Prometheus remote write compatible): HTTPS/443 to your metrics endpoint or to our collector in VPC.
   - Tracing: OTLP/HTTP or OTLP/gRPC depending on your collector; default: OTLP/HTTP on 4318.
   - Allowlist: we'll provide a stable set of IPs for Dedicated but for Private deploys we provide a short list per customer that can change with scaling; suggest allowing an FQDN and a CIDR fallback.

3) Connection model: persistent keepalive pools with TLS session reuse. We also support a buffered retry queue on disk (encrypted) for transient network interruptions — helpful for short intermittent outages.

4) Headers & mapping:
   - We propagate traceparent (W3C) and b3 headers. If you require x-cloud-trace-context we can map it from traceparent.
   - We'll include a mapping CSV showing field -> Splunk sourcetype keys.

5) Evidence & audit:
   - Forwarding log: each egress bundle includes a signed metadata record (timestamp, forwarder id, file hash) which you can fetch for audit.

Action items:
- Kimberly: share the preliminary CIDR list and VPC flow diagram (done).
- Acme: confirm whether you want mTLS or HEC tokens.
- Schedule handshake: Kimberly proposed Mon Jul 29 11:00 UTC.

Attachments: splunk_hec_runbook.md, tracehook_header_matrix.csv

— Marissa
Staff Software Engineer, Observability Integrations

FWIW: attached is a short compliance checklist we've used with other regulated customers and an example evidence bundle procedure. Key items for your audit team:

- Acceptance criteria for ingestion: sample payloads, sourcetypes, and schema mapping (we'll provide Splunk props and transforms snippets).
- Proof of custody: signed forwarding metadata (as Marissa noted) + periodic snapshot of retention config.
- Scrubbing rules: example redaction rules for email, SSNs, and credit card patterns; we support both inbound and pre‑egress redaction.
- Airgap mode: if your deployment is air‑gapped we support an offline evidence collector that writes a signed bundle to an operator USB/secure transfer host.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_vpc_flow_diagram.pdf, compliance_checklist_acme.md

I'll be on the call Monday to cover the audit artifacts.

— Mina
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
